templates.name: Minimal Professional
templates.tagline: Clean ink-on-cream one-pager with a sticky nav and a calm, trustworthy voice.
templates.best_for: Anyone who needs to read as competent and low-risk to hire or partner with: consultants, freelancers, advisors, B2B SaaS one-pagers, professional personal brands. Works equally well as a CV page or a lightweight company homepage.
templates.avoid_for: Contexts that want to feel loud, experimental, or overtly creative — the restrained palette and grid intentionally stay out of the way of the content.

templates.name: Bold Creative
templates.tagline: Neo-brutalist one-pager: thick borders, offset shadows, one neon-lime accent on off-white.
templates.best_for: Indie founders, creative freelancers, and small startups who want to land as confident and memorable rather than corporate. Strong for a business-idea pitch page or a designer/developer's personal site.
templates.avoid_for: Contexts that need institutional restraint or quiet credibility — the thick borders and neon accent commit hard to a graphic, opinionated voice.

templates.name: Warm Editorial
templates.tagline: Serif-led magazine feel on warm paper, sage and rust accents, story-first structure.
occasion: consultant bio with a point of view
templates.best_for: People and small studios whose story is the pitch: writers, coaches, therapists, consultants with a point of view, boutique studios. Leads with narrative before it leads with credentials.
templates.avoid_for: Contexts that need to feel fast, technical, or heavily data-driven — the serif/paper treatment is intentionally slow and personal.

templates.name: Dark Tech Modern
templates.tagline: Dark canvas with a violet-to-cyan glow, built to pitch a product or business idea.
templates.best_for: Tech founders and developers pitching a product, a company, or themselves with a technical edge. The problem → solution → features structure is built for a business-idea pitch, not just a bio.
templates.avoid_for: Warm, personal, or traditional contexts — the dark gradient canvas reads as startup-technical, not intimate or institutional.

templates.name: Corporate Pitch
templates.tagline: Navy-and-white corporate one-pager with a trusted-by strip and a leadership grid.
templates.best_for: Companies and executives who need to read as established and low-risk: enterprise sales pages, investor one-pagers, agency capabilities pages, executive bios. The trusted-by strip and leadership grid are built for institutional credibility.
templates.avoid_for: Contexts that want to feel indie, experimental, or personal — the navy palette and grid structure read as corporate by design.

templates.name: Playful Personal
templates.tagline: Rounded pastel blobs, bouncy display type, and a friendly, human voice.
templates.best_for: Creators, coaches, small-business owners, and community brands who want to feel warm and human rather than corporate. Great for a first personal site or a hobby turning into a small business.
templates.avoid_for: Contexts that need institutional gravitas — the rounded shapes and bright palette are intentionally informal.

templates.name: Luxury Portfolio
templates.tagline: Near-black canvas, gold hairlines, italic serif display — a gallery-quality portfolio page.
templates.best_for: Photographers, architects, designers, and luxury brands where the visuals are the pitch. Generous whitespace and a large image gallery let the work carry the page.
templates.avoid_for: Content-heavy pages or contexts needing lots of text per screen — the layout is built around large images and short, considered copy.

templates.name: Academic CV
templates.tagline: Structured, serif-set CV page: timeline, publications, and a résumé download button.
templates.best_for: Academics, researchers, and job-seekers who need a dense, structured, print-friendly alternative to a PDF résumé — timeline-based experience, a publications list, and a résumé-download CTA.
templates.avoid_for: Brand or business pages where visual personality matters more than information density — this template is built to be read, not browsed.

templates.name: Technical Sidebar Profile
templates.tagline: Monospace, carbon-and-accent engineer homepage: dark profile sidebar, hero card with stats, a numbered delivery-stage timeline, work history, chip-dense skill cards, and education. One --accent variable recolours it, --font switches mono/sans, and it prints as a clean PDF résumé.
occasion: ML or platform engineer personal site
templates.best_for: Hands-on technical ICs (AI forward deployed engineers, solution and pre-sales architects, field engineers, ML and platform engineers) who want to show end-to-end delivery, work history, and a specific skill stack on one information-only page. Stage names, skill cards, and social/contact channels are all placeholders that adapt to any technical specialty; recolour by changing --accent (use a bright accent, and set --on-accent to white for dark ones).
templates.avoid_for: Non-technical, warm, or brand-led pages: the monospace type and dense chip lists read as an engineer's spec sheet. Also a poor fit for anyone with few concrete proof points, since the stages and outcomes lean on real results.

templates.name: Playful Dev Folio
templates.tagline: Friendly Montserrat-and-purple developer portfolio: waving greeting, skill icons, proficiency bars, brand-colored experience cards, and a dark-mode toggle.
occasion: developer with talks and blog posts
templates.best_for: Developers who want a warm, personality-forward portfolio covering a lot of ground: skills, experience, open source, certifications, writing, and talks on one page. Ships with a light/dark toggle.
templates.avoid_for: Senior, executive, or formal contexts, and anyone with little to put in its many sections. The proficiency bars are self-assessed, so drop them if the user has no estimate of their own.

templates.name: Mono Minimal Dev
templates.tagline: All-monospace minimalist portfolio: oversized 'I'm [Name]' hero in blue, titles-left section rows, numbered project cards, and a dot timeline.
templates.best_for: Engineers who want a quiet, typographic page where the work speaks: IBM Plex Mono throughout, lots of whitespace, one blue accent, and a clean projects → experience → education flow.
templates.avoid_for: Visual or creative portfolios that need imagery (there are no image slots), and non-technical audiences, for whom the all-monospace type can read as cold.

templates.name: Illustrated Sky Folio
templates.tagline: Pale sky-blue, navy-ink portfolio built around big illustrations: signature-script logo, alternating 'What I Do?' rows with tech badges and ⚡ bullets, and light-blue project tiles.
templates.best_for: Developers who work across several areas (e.g. AI, full-stack, cloud, design) and want each one to get its own illustrated row. It looks best when the user supplies flat illustrations or photos for the large 4:3 image slots.
templates.avoid_for: Users with no images at all: the layout leans on its illustration slots, which stay as placeholders otherwise. Also a poor fit for formal or senior positioning.

templates.name: Bold Blue Folio
templates.tagline: Full-screen blue hero with a triangle pattern and uppercase headline, a fixed social rail, laptop-mockup project rows, and a contact form on a blue band.
templates.best_for: Freelancers and frontend developers selling to clients: a big first impression, a short about, three or so projects shown as screenshots in laptop frames with case-study links, and a contact form. The form needs no backend; it opens the visitor's email app with the message filled in.
templates.avoid_for: Content-heavy profiles (many roles, publications, certifications), since it's deliberately sparse. Also a poor fit when there are no project screenshots for the laptop frames.

templates.name: GitHub Card Profile
templates.tagline: Dashboard-style profile on a grey canvas: a left column of info cards (avatar, details, tech stack, mini timelines) and right-hand panels of repo, publication, project, and article cards.
templates.best_for: Developers whose best proof is their repositories, papers, and posts, who want everything visible at a glance with no scrolling story. The repo cards are static HTML: fill them with the user's real repo names, descriptions, star counts, and languages.
templates.avoid_for: Visual, brand-led, or non-technical pages, and anyone without public repos or writing to show. It has no hero or narrative section.
